newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania in no hurry to end the dollar peg.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania in no hurry to end the dollar peg.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank on Wednesday said an end to its litas currency peg with the dollar would take around two years to introduce and that ideas for the change were only in the very initial stages.
A new monetary strategy was aired on Tuesday by central bank policy department head Gintanas Nauseda, who said the litas may eventually be pegged to the dollar and the mark.
But central bank deputy governor Jonas Niaura said any changes would take time.
"It is not official bank policy, it is only a draft policy," Niauras told Reuters, speaking of Gintanas' remarks.
"It may take two years or more to implement," he added.
The litas is currently pegged at four to the dollar under a currency board system.
The new right-wing government wants to end the peg and scrap the currency board and the central bank has been looking at ways the changes could be made.
Gintanas' comment was the first open comment from a central bank official at what was being planned.
He said that eventually the litas may be pegged only to the mark, which is to become the monetary anchor for the new European currency.
"We are looking at long-term ways to remove the currency board and eventually integrate it with the European monetary unit," Niaura added.
"It is still hard to say at this moment what currencies we will tie the litas to," he said.
Under the currency board, the central bank has to keep enough reserves in its vaults to back the local currency circulation but it has no powers to influence monetary policy.
The new government says the currency board peg has led to an inflexible monetary system that has over-valued the litas.
